Construct a Reproducibility Manifest

Source: R/lib_manifest.R
mkmnf.Rd

Creates an empty manifest: the record of one analysis run that collects the run's metadata, the cross-checks of its results against expected values (added with recrd()), and optionally a snapshot of the R environment it ran in. Write it out with wrmnfjs() and wrsmrytxt(), or hash and sign it with mnfdgst() and cpsatst(), so a reader can later see what was run, where, and whether the numbers matched.

Usage

mkmnf(meta, env = TRUE)

Arguments

meta

A list of run metadata, normally named (for example project, author, run_at, synthetic). May be list().

env

Logical scalar; when TRUE (the default) the manifest also records the analysis environment via capenv(): R version, platform, OS, UTC timestamp, random number generator kind and whether it was seeded, and the version of every loaded package. Any other value leaves it out.

Value

A list with elements meta (the list given, plus synthetic = TRUE when flagged), results (an empty list, filled by recrd()) and, when environment = TRUE, environment (the list from capenv()).

Details

The manifest is a plain list, so you can add your own elements to meta before writing it. The package owns the synthetic-data flag: meta$synthetic is set to TRUE when you pass it, when the environment variable BRICKLAYER_SYNTHETIC is set to a value other than 0, false, no or off, or when the package generated synthetic data earlier in the session. It is written only when TRUE, so a manifest of real data keeps the digest it had before the flag existed. On a synthetic manifest every recrd() entry is INFO.

The fields of meta that wrsmrytxt() reads are project, author, run_at, os, r_version and, as a named list or vector of versions, r_package_versions.

Errors when meta is not a list. Nothing is written.

See also

recrd(), wrmnfjs(), wrsmrytxt(), mnfdgst().

Examples

# Minimal manifest, no environment capture.
man <- mkmnf(list(project = "demo-study", author = "A. Author"),
  env = FALSE
)
names(man) # "meta" "results"
#> [1] "meta"    "results"
man$meta$project
#> [1] "demo-study"

# With environment = TRUE it also records R version / platform / packages.
full <- mkmnf(list(project = "demo"), env = TRUE)
names(full) # adds "environment"
#> [1] "meta"        "results"     "environment"
full$environment$r_version
#> [1] "4.6.1"

# a run on generated data is flagged, and its checks become INFO
syn <- mkmnf(list(project = "demo", synthetic = TRUE), env = FALSE)
syn$meta$synthetic
#> [1] TRUE

# meta must be a list
try(mkmnf("demo"))
#> Error : `meta` must be a list
